ai.title: Add mockModule wrapper for module mocking
ai.summary: Added `mockModule` and `clearMockedModules` in `common/src/testing/mock-modules.ts`. `mockModule` wraps `bun:test` `mock.module` to cache originals and support nested mocks, replacing direct `mock.module` calls in `evals/scaffolding.ts`. `clearMockedModules` restores originals, used in `afterAll` hooks per `knowledge.md` guidance.

eli5.text: The software's testing tools now have a new helper that makes it easier to temporarily swap out parts of the system during automated tests. Instead of directly replacing code modules (which could accidentally break other tests or leave things in a wrong state), tests now go through this single, safer method that keeps track of the original code and automatically restores it when the test finishes. This change affects the test suite used by the development team and is already in place across many test files.

ai.title: Fix usage-calculation test mock path
ai.summary: Corrected mock path in `usage-calculation.test.ts` from `@codebuff/common/db/index` to `@codebuff/common/db`. Aligns test setup with actual module resolution. Internal test fix only.

eli5.text: Nothing for you to see here. The team fixed a small mistake in a behind-the-scenes test that checks the assistant's usage calculations, correcting a path reference so the test setup matches how the code actually loads. Because it only touches the testing tools, not the running service, it has no effect on what you experience today.

ai.title: Remove global agentRegistry from backend
ai.summary: Replaced the global AgentRegistry class with a stateless getAllAgentTemplates function returning a plain object. AsyncAgentManager and mainPrompt now fetch templates per request, passing the registry explicitly to loopAgentSteps and runAgentStep. Deleted unused agent-system-prompt.ts.

eli5.text: The backend now builds each assistant's set of available helpers fresh on every request instead of keeping one shared list stored globally. If you use the chat, you won't see any visible difference, but internally the code is cleaner and won't carry leftover state between your conversations. One unused instruction file was also deleted, and the system now checks for valid assistants at the moment it needs them rather than trusting an always-on registry.

ai.title: Fix duplicate parameters in tool renderer
ai.summary: Refactored `parsePartialJsonObject` to accept raw previous content string instead of parsed object, enabling accurate delta calculation for streaming tool parameters. Added `parsePartialJsonObjectSingle` for internal use and updated `getPartialJsonDelta` to compare against previous raw content, preventing duplicate parameter emission when partial JSON chunks overlap. Updated `xml-stream-parser.ts` to pass `prevParamsContent` to `getPartialJsonDelta`. Covers `common/src/util/partial-json-delta.ts` and `npm-app/src/utils/xml-stream-parser.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant streams its replies that include tool calls, you sometimes saw the same parameter appear twice. That happened because the system compared each new piece of a tool's input against an already-interpreted version of the prior piece, so overlapping bits got counted again. It now compares each incoming piece against the raw text of what came before, so no parameter is repeated. If you watched a streaming tool call, you would no longer see duplicated keys; the fix is live today.

ai.title: Replace updatereport with setoutput tool
ai.summary: The `update_report` tool is removed and replaced by `set_output` for structured agent responses. Agent templates now use `outputMode: 'json'` instead of `'report'`, and the `git-committer` agent model switched to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4`. Dynamic agent templates support optional `outputSchema` fields converted to Zod, defaulting `outputMode` to `'json'` when present. Core files updated: `backend/src/tools/definitions/set-output.ts`, `backend/src/templates/dynamic-agent-service.ts`, `backend/src/templates/agents/base.ts`, `backend/src/run-programmatic-step.ts`.

eli5.text: The way the code-writing helper gives you its final answer has changed: it used to send you a formatted report, and now it sends you a structured JSON output instead. If you watched an agent work, you would see it end its turn slightly differently and produce a machine-friendly summary rather than a narrative one. The git-committer agent also switched to a different AI provider (Claude Sonnet 4), and templates that define optional output fields now default to JSON mode automatically. This is live today and affects any template or consumer reading the agent's output state.

ai.title: Update partial-json-delta tests for streaming
ai.summary: Rewrote `getPartialJsonDelta` tests in `common/src/util/__tests__/partial-json-delta.test.ts` to strictly validate streaming input contracts and `lastParam` tracking. Previous tests incorrectly passed parsed objects as `previous` state; new tests enforce string-prefix validation and verify delta extraction for multi-line strings and non-string types. Scope limited to `common` package unit tests.

eli5.text: If you watched the assistant respond to your questions piece by piece (streaming), the behind-the-scenes test that checked how each fragment was understood has been rewritten. The old checks mistakenly fed already-parsed data instead of raw text fragments, so the checks could pass while real streaming input was handled incorrectly. The new checks always require the raw text fragment to be a true prefix of the prior text, and they verify that partial words in multi-line answers and non-text values (like numbers) are tracked correctly; this is test-only housekeeping and does not change what you see, but it helps catch streaming-response bugs earlier.

ai.title: Input validation in getPartialJsonDelta
ai.summary: Added explicit error throwing in `getPartialJsonDelta` when `content` does not start with `previous`. Prevents invalid partial JSON delta calculations. Affects `common/src/util/partial-json-delta.ts`.

eli5.text: The software that pieces together partial updates to your conversation now checks that each new chunk of text properly follows the previous one. If a chunk doesn't build on what came before it (for example, if the connection drops and data arrives out of order), the system will raise a clear error instead of silently producing a garbled response. You would only notice this if something went wrong with streaming your reply, in which case you'd see an error rather than a broken message. This is already live today.

ai.title: Version 1.0.438
ai.summary: Version bumped to 1.0.438. Updates `codebuff` package metadata.

eli5.text: If you use the AI coding assistant, updating to this version lets it run specialized helper agents inside your code (through a new /subagent command), inspect detailed step-by-step logs with a --trace flag, and manage conversation history more reliably. Behind the scenes, the system now handles agent steps and tool calls in a cleaner way and can safely pause or skip work if you cancel. The change is live today if you update the app.

ai.title: partial-json-delta skips brace completion for numeric ends
ai.summary: parsePartialJsonObjectSingle now checks if content ends with a digit before attempting to append a closing brace. This prevents malformed JSON errors when parsing partial objects that terminate in numeric values. The change applies to common/src/util/partial-json-delta.ts. The fallback logic for closing quotes remains unaffected.

eli5.text: When you're typing something that looks like the beginning of a data object and the text ends with a number, the system now leaves it alone instead of trying to automatically close it off. Before this fix, if your text ended in a number and the system added a closing bracket, it would create broken data that couldn't be read. You'd notice this when working with streaming data that stops mid-number - it now waits instead of forcing a broken completion.

ai.title: Refactor partial JSON delta parsing logic
ai.summary: Refactored `getPartialJsonDelta` in `common/src/util/partial-json-delta.ts` to inline previous parse logic, removing the `parsePartialJsonObject` helper. Added `delta[lastKey] === undefined` check in `npm-app/src/utils/xml-stream-parser.ts` to prevent overwriting existing delta values. Scope limited to core utility and stream parser.

eli5.text: The system now handles messy, half-finished data chunks more reliably when they arrive in pieces. Previously, if a multi-part data chunk arrived while another was still being read, the system could mix them up and overwrite good data with stale bits; now it checks whether that piece already has a real value before touching it, leaving intact values untouched. You won't see a flashy new feature, but streaming data that previously glitched or dropped fields will now assemble correctly on screen. The change is purely behind the scenes, like quietly reorganizing how puzzle pieces are sorted so the picture comes together right the first time.

Renames endsAgentStepParam from codebuff_end_step to codebuff_easp across tools.ts and constants/tools.ts. Adds MALFORMED_TOOL_CALL_JSON and UNKNOWN_TOOL_CALL analytics events in xml-stream-parser.ts and analytics-events.ts. Tool executor now conditionally extends schema only when endsAgentStep is true.

eli5.text: When you chat with an AI assistant that uses special tools (like web search), the system now sends better signals about when a tool is being used and when an AI step should wrap up, making the assistant's responses more reliable and its actions easier to track. Under the hood, the software switched from a list of stop signals to a single, clearer one and added new analytics to catch errors when tool calls are malformed or unknown tools are referenced, which helps developers spot and fix problems faster. If you looked at the logs, you'd notice fewer ambiguous tool-call messages and more precise timing around when steps end, plus new background events logged if the assistant tries to use a tool it can't handle. ai.title: Add AGENTSPROMPT placeholder to agent templates
ai.summary: Introduce AGENTS_PROMPT placeholder in backend/src/templates/types.ts and populate it via buildSpawnableAgentsDescription in new file backend/src/templates/prompts.ts. This replaces the previous approach of injecting agent descriptions directly into tool instructions, now handled by separate logic in backend/src/tools/prompts.ts. Scope includes core agent templates (planner, researcher, reviewer, etc.) and base/ask prompts, ensuring all agents can dynamically list spawnable subagents. The change decouples tool definitions from agent availability, allowing cleaner circular dependency resolution in backend/src/tools.ts.

eli5.text: Each helper your main assistant can summon (planner, researcher, reviewer, etc.) now receives a clear, automatically updated roster of the other helpers that exist, so when one of them decides to call for backup it sees the same current list instead of a stale, hard-typed one. Behind the scenes, the list is generated once and plugged into every helper's instructions, and the wiring that previously tangled tools to specific helpers was loosened, letting the system keep everyone in sync without circular references. The result you'd notice is fewer 'agent not found' surprises and helpers that more consistently know which teammates are available to be spawned.
